title: Yuvraj Singh Says India Must Give Young Batters ODI Chances
excerpt: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh says leaving Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi out of 50-over cricket does not do justice to their talent, while conceding competition for places is fierce.
body:
• Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh says leaving Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi out of 50-over cricket does not do justice to their talent.
  • Yuvraj, a long-time mentor to Abhishek, spoke to PTI on the sidelines of the Protocol 32 launch event.
  • Kishan has played 32 ODIs, while Abhishek and Sooryavanshi have never been called up to India's ODI setup despite their T20I form.
  • Yuvraj conceded competition for places is fierce, but said the young batters' performances should put them in the ODI squad soon.

Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh has said India are not doing justice to the talent of Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi by leaving them out of the one-day international setup, in comments reported by CricTracker and CREX.

Yuvraj spoke to PTI on the sidelines of the Protocol 32 launch event. He has served as a long-time mentor to Abhishek, and his backing carried a direct message for the selectors ahead of India's five-match ODI series against New Zealand, which opens at Eden Park in Auckland on November 4.

"If we are not picking guys like Ishan Kishan, Abhishek and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in 50-over cricket, then somewhere down the line we are not doing justice to their talent."

— Yuvraj Singh, former India all-rounder

Three batters, three different cases

The three players Yuvraj named are at different stages. Kishan has already played 32 ODIs for India, and his most recent appearance in the format came on July 19, 2026, against England. Abhishek and Sooryavanshi, by contrast, have never been handed a call-up to the ODI setup, even though both have featured in India's recent T20I squad for the New Zealand tour.

Abhishek's List A record gives Yuvraj's argument a statistical base: the opener has played 69 List A matches, scoring 2,196 runs at a strike rate of 100.18. Sooryavanshi's case rests on a rapid rise through age-group and senior cricket — he made his international debut in a T20I series in England, helped India U19 to the 2026 ICC U19 World Cup title in Zimbabwe, and holds one of the fastest List A centuries on record, an 84-ball 190 for Bihar.

A mentor's backing, with a caveat

Yuvraj was careful to acknowledge the other side of the selection problem. India have a settled group of senior players, places in the ODI squad are limited, and breaking into the side is hard for any young batter. "I understand we have some great players and it is hard to make a spot for them. I think the way they are performing, they should be in the squad soon, hopefully," he said.

He also placed Abhishek's rise on the player himself, saying whatever the opener has achieved is the result of his own hard work. That distinction matters coming from a mentor: Yuvraj is arguing for an opportunity, not claiming one is owed.

Why the timing matters

India are settling on a core group for the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup, which makes every ODI squad from here a signal about who is inside the selectors' long-term plans and who is outside them. Leaving three attacking left-hand options out of the 50-over picture entirely, Yuvraj argues, wastes the time those players need to learn the longer white-ball format at international level before a World Cup cycle peaks.

For Indian fans in the diaspora following the New Zealand tour, the debate is a familiar one: a team rich in batting talent has to choose between continuity with proven ODI performers and early investment in the batters dominating T20 cricket. Yuvraj, a World Cup winner in 2011, has made his position plain — the talent is ready to be tested, and the testing ground has to be the ODI squad itself.
